qt: to the Commission Ştefan Muşoiu (S&D) Subject:

The EU is founded on values such as democracy, the rule of law, gender equality, freedom of expression, respect for human rights and tolerance. Article 2 of the Treaty on European Union (TEU) enshrines respect for human dignity, freedom, democracy, equality, the rule of law and respect for human rights. At the same time, Article 79 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) provides for the development of a common immigration policy, including the integration of non-EU nationals. However, the cultural differences between immigrants and the peoples of the Union make it necessary to strengthen the scope of European policy concerning their integration, going beyond the predominantly administrative and socio-economic approach and explicitly including ownership of the EU’s fundamental values, the principles of the rule of law, gender equality, freedom of conscience and expression, and the democratic and secular nature of public institutions, where these are enshrined in the national constitutional order. Given that the Commission is responsible for coordinating European integration strategies, I would like to ask it to clarify whether it intends to optimise these European policies, which are based on mutual respect and ownership of our values, so that cultural diversity is protected and European citizens are not directly or indirectly forced to live in a way that is contrary to the values, freedoms and democratic traditions of the societies in which they were born and live.
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (29.10.2026) The integration of migrants is primarily a national competence, while the EU supports, coordinates and complements Member States’ efforts in this field. The Action Plan on integration and inclusion 2021-20271 forms the basis of the Commission action and lays down measures to support Member States in migrants’ integration, notably by facilitating access to education, the labour market, housing, healthcare and language learning. The Action Plan also Member States in promoting mutual respect and understanding, inclusion and participation in community life with the aim to develop cohesive societies. The Commission approach is based on the respect for the values set out in Article 2 of the Treaty on European Union (TEU), including human dignity, freedom, democracy, equality, the rule of law and respect for human rights, as guaranteed under the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the EU. Integration policy also aims at mainstreaming gender equality and antidiscrimination. As recalled by the European Asylum and Migration Management Strategy2 adopted in January 2026, the respect of the values laid down in Article 2 TEU is a central element for the successful integration of migrants. The Commission will therefore continue to work closely with Member States to promote integration policies that are inclusive, effective and rooted in the EU’s common values. In that regard, several Member States have put in place civic learning programmes to ensure that migrants understand and respect the culture of their host society, including via the use of pre-departure orientation courses.
1 Communication from the Commission to the European Parliament, the Council, the European Economic and

Social Committee and the Committee of the Regions - Action plan on Integration and Inclusion 2021-2027 (COM/2020/758 final); https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52020DC0758. 2 Communication from the Commission to the European Parliament and the Council - European Asylum and Migration Management Strategy (COM/2026/45 final); https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legalcontent/EN/TXT/?uri=celex:52026DC0045.
